613353.name: Deduction.ch_core
613353.title: Average over characters
613353.statement: Under the size and character hypotheses, per-index discrepancy bounds imply a power bound for GmA up to SigA.
613353.role: Character orthogonality and scale estimates convert the indexed bounds into a weighted average.

613360.name: Deduction.ch_top
613360.title: Bound the discrepancy per index
613360.statement: The named identifications and size, error, and norm windows give an upper bound for gapA.
613360.role: Write gapA as ASK minus Main, then combine the per-index estimate and the error bracket.

613413.name: Deduction.landau_window
613413.title: Rule out a pole right of θ
613413.statement: For the supplied PoleData and WindowHypU, any ρ in the specified pole set satisfies Re(ρ)≤θ.
613413.role: Use high derivatives to compare a window upper bound with growth from an isolated pole.

613417.name: Deduction.lemmaL
613417.title: Apply the pole obstruction
613417.statement: WindowHyp on a finite character family implies ZeroFree F θ in the given parameter range.
613417.role: Build the pole data, exclude zeros in the strip by the window lemma, and use established nonvanishing at Re(s)≥1.

613458.name: Deduction.poleData
613458.title: Poles of the finite-family transform
613458.statement: For each admissible finite family there exists a transform with PoleData for its zero set.
613458.role: Assemble individual character transforms and their pole data using positive weights.

613405.name: Deduction.zeroFree_of_rpow_window
613405.title: The character-family power-window theorem
613405.statement: For a positive-weight family, a one-sided x^θ bound on arbitrarily late [Y,Y^(1+δ)] implies ZeroFree F θ.
613405.role: Pass to the weighted-integral formulation of the Landau window criterion.

924105.name: Formalism.F.slopeInequality_of
924105.title: The lattice slope inequality
924105.statement: The sublattice bound SlopeLeMuMax implies SlopeInequality for injective norm-bounded lattice maps.
924105.role: A Gram determinant bounds the image covolume by C to the rank times the source covolume.

868671.name: Formalism.FrobeniusOrbits.ThickExists.noRel_image
868671.title: Behrend’s collision-free indices
868671.statement: For L≥1, encoding an integer sphere in base 4Ld gives a set with NoRel for coefficients bounded by L.
868671.role: The large base avoids carries. A line meets a sphere in at most two distinct points.

1126697.name: Formalism.HC.ChebyshevInequalityAtWindowScale
1126697.title: Uniform families on power windows
1126697.statement: There exist eD,eL and ε₁>0 such that every 0<ε<ε₁ admits a tied family with whole windows of width λ.
1126697.role: The loss exponents are uniform in epsilon. The family may vary with epsilon.

1125868.name: Formalism.HC.Level.Gm
1125868.title: The weighted prime sum
1125868.statement: G_P(x)=Gζ(x) plus a finite weighted sum of real parts of twisted smoothed errors.
1125868.role: The cyclic level gives every nontrivial primitive inducing character weight 1/(3o+1).

1126696.name: Formalism.HC.level_of_tiedWin
1126696.title: Choose epsilon after a candidate zero
1126696.statement: At any level, the chosen uniform arithmetic window and the analytic criterion imply zero-freeness right of one half.
1126696.role: Take θ strictly between one half and the candidate real part, then choose ε with the loss exponent below θ.

1126701.name: Formalism.HC.zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin
1126701.title: Pass from levels to characters
1126701.statement: Appropriate level data for each ψ satisfying Q imply ZeroFreeOn Q.
1126701.role: Extract the appropriate level and invoke level_of_tiedWin.

1126702.name: Formalism.HC.zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin_cyc
1126702.title: Assemble the cyclic levels
1126702.statement: Uniform window bounds, FormB, and family existence for cyclic levels imply ZeroFreeOn Q.
1126702.role: A primitive character belongs to its own cyclic level, so the level criterion covers it.

872844.name: Formalism.HermitianLattices.GL2a2.PsiZeroConst
872844.title: The first moment of the Chebyshev error
872844.statement: The truncated integral of (ψ(t)−t)/t² from 1 to U tends to −1−γ as U tends to infinity.
872844.role: This is an improper-integral limit for the real von Mangoldt sum. It fixes the coefficient of the linear centering term in the reading converse.

872698.name: Formalism.HermitianLattices.GL2a2.psi_zero_integral_constant
872698.title: Evaluate the first moment
872698.statement: The archive supplies its first-moment limit without an RH assumption.
872698.role: The public theorem calls the source-level proof psiZeroConst_main. This separate theorem helps explain the reverse implication for the singleton zeta family.

949673.name: Formalism.L2.G.linkG_concrete5
949673.title: Local and orbit bounds for compatible families
949673.statement: On a family class with group compatibility and the second admissibility condition, the conclusion bundles eventual local length and inert-prime estimates together with orbit containment and the mean kappa bound.
949673.role: The caller establishes compatibility and admissibility for its restricted family class and combines them here to obtain LinkG.

1086379.name: Formalism.MainNotions.ColumnSystems.Pf.key_minor_dvd
1086379.title: A local source of divisibility
1086379.statement: For w²=p and the displayed congruences, w divides a two-by-two minor.
1086379.role: In the quotient by w the two transformed rows are multiples of one row. Their minor vanishes.

665153.name: GlobalTheory.BigOn.ontoX_of_hypotheses_alt_alt
665153.title: Eventual bounds at twisted places
665153.statement: For an eligible family satisfying DIVinN, the arithmetic and representation hypotheses give a common threshold. At sufficiently late qualifying points, the twisted-place sums and their weighted errors satisfy the ON inequalities for every parameter above that threshold.
665153.role: The unitary-group caller supplies these hypotheses from its third-place package and pairs the resulting bounds with a separate lower bound for lambda.

296640.name: GlobalTheory.CarrierGap.offDiag
296640.title: Off-diagonal kernel bounds for distinct words
296640.statement: Under the mass, positivity and finite-dimensional row hypotheses, local ties, rank control and a loop bound give the eventual estimate for the squared norm of the selected off-diagonal kernel at distinct words.
296640.role: The selection theorem combines this off-diagonal bound with a loop bound and the torsion-free condition.

727318.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Cusp.volumeTheoremX_of_inputs
727318.title: Volume and slope estimates for CM towers
727318.statement: Given the geometry, integrability, Weil, Hodge flag, degree, twisting and comparison inputs, the specified root towers over abelian CM fields satisfy the volume identities and uniform slope estimates under their size and bad-place bounds.
727318.role: The caller re-exports these tower estimates from the same geometric inputs.

780730.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Link.good_tower_volume_theorem_bis
780730.title: Good towers and their volume estimates
780730.statement: The arithmetic intersection, Hilbert–Samuel, bigness, resolution, extension, Hodge–Tate, GAGA, large-degree line, quotient and Zarhin hypotheses give both good-tower existence and the tower volume theorem.
780730.role: The caller uses the pair of tower results in the proof of the deep-model mean-slope bound.

780728.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Plug.deepStR_of_use
780728.title: Lower bound for mean volume slopes
780728.statement: The stated intersection, positivity and arithmetic-geometric inputs give a uniform lower bound, with weighted error, for the mean of component volume slopes on eligible deep models with at most fifteen specified prime factors.
780728.role: The caller builds the intersection and resolution inputs and applies this estimate to obtain its deep-model bound.

726488.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Top.goodTower_and_volume
726488.title: Good root towers and volume estimates
726488.statement: The packaged geometric inputs, integrability, avoidance, Weil statement, positive family and comparison pair imply both good root tower existence and uniform volume and slope estimates.
726488.role: The exported tower theorem uses this result directly to supply both conclusions together.

731922.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Top.goodTower_volume_of_reduced
731922.title: Root towers and volume from geometric inputs
731922.statement: Toroidal compatibility, the key formula and the listed height, comparison and uniformization hypotheses yield good root towers and the tower volume theorem.
731922.role: The exported right-hand input theorem uses this implication directly, with the same assumptions and conclusions.

67060.name: GlobalTheory.EX.RankVal
67060.title: The geometric ranks
67060.statement: In particular, sqrt(x δ₁)≤m≤2 sqrt(x δ₁), with δ₁=x^(−ε/8).
67060.role: The precise fixed-epsilon rank scale is x^(1/2−ε/16).

664499.name: GlobalTheory.Fam.miAt_of_truePack_alt_alt
664499.title: Inner-product identity for one real package
664499.statement: The listed automorphic hypotheses and a realized TruePackAlt imply the coefficient-space inner-product identity with norm-preserving data and nonzero factors, assuming positive rank parameter and the PuNZ nonvanishing condition.
664499.role: Its caller exports the same real-package implication directly as a published-input theorem.

664497.name: GlobalTheory.Fam.miStar2_of_allTrue_alt_alt
664497.title: Isometric periods from family conditions
664497.statement: For a real package built from the given member data, the representation-theoretic hypotheses, all family conditions, a positive rank parameter and nonvanishing local period values yield isometric period data with nonzero coefficients.
664497.role: The caller re-exports this pointwise implication under its published-results theorem name.

664506.name: GlobalTheory.Fam.miStar_row_alt_alt
664506.title: Bundle point conditions imply period identities
664506.statement: Given the representation-theoretic inputs, diagonal scale-and-rank condition and parameter-point witnesses, the bundle point conditions imply the isometric period identity with nonzero coefficients along the row.
664506.role: The caller re-exports this implication with the same hypotheses and conclusion.

668223.name: GlobalTheory.Fam.volLev_mul_wt_mid_alt
668223.title: An existence check on a period identity
668223.statement: At a suitable intermediate stage there exists v≠0 such that level volume times character weight equals v at every admissible datum.
668223.role: Haar measure times index is constant. When the permitted datum set is empty the theorem explicitly chooses v=1.

663931.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.AllAtMemberStage0.allRows_of_open0_alt
663931.title: Assemble the definite-side rows
663931.statement: Given the reciprocity and representation-theoretic inputs, the twisted-place inequalities and a lower bound on log λ, the open parameter conditions and linked covolume, functional and norm conditions produce all the rows required on the definite side.
663931.role: The caller feeds these rows to the construction of a nonempty definite-side hypothesis package.
663931.caption: Norm and covolume conditions on the definite side

665156.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.S0.Open0ProofU.open_orbit_of_unramified_exponents_alt
665156.title: Construct the open parameter conditions
665156.statement: The third-place unitary-group hypotheses give the package of open parameter conditions for every permitted local Langlands parameter choice and real dependence constant.
665156.role: The caller re-exports this package for the same dependence parameters under its unitary-group theorem name.

662912.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.S0.StageU.hypotheses_nonempty_of_unramified_exponents_alt
662912.title: Assemble the definite-side hypotheses
662912.statement: The third-place unitary hypotheses, rationality row, local parameter convention, eventual largeness and linked norm, functional and covolume bounds give an instance of the definite-side hypotheses.
662912.role: The caller chooses a grid and a common threshold, then supplies its functional and covolume estimates to this assembly step.
662912.caption: Unramified exponents in the definite-side estimates

667650.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.S0.ontoX_and_lamLow_of_unitaryGroupHypotheses'
667650.title: Twisted-place bounds and a log λ lower bound
667650.statement: The third-place unitary-group hypotheses give both the eventual twisted-place inequalities and the eventual lower bound on log λ for the eligible families.
667650.role: The caller extracts both conclusions and passes them separately into the construction of all definite-side rows.

664639.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.StageOneU.member_bundles_large_unramified_exponents_alt
664639.title: Mass ratio and linked member bundles
664639.statement: The third-place unitary hypotheses, rational row test, existence of local parameters and an eventually large retwisting condition give the CM Siegel mass ratio, membership conditions and existence of linked bundles for the constructed extension.
664639.role: The caller exports this same three-part assertion about the extension.

667082.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.forall_goal_of_shape_of_hyps
667082.title: Apply the shape to the same chosen data
667082.statement: For propositions V, NR, G and a class predicate N, take TopShapeAlt V NR N G, V, NR and HypsAlt N DefiniteSideCondition to G.
667082.role: For the primitive zero-free argument both auxiliary propositions are trivial. The concrete input is the chosen definite-side record.

667083.name: GlobalTheory.Fc.goal_of_shape_of_hyps
667083.title: Supply the actual fields of the shape
667083.statement: TopShapeAlt V NR N G with V, NR and HypsAlt N DefiniteSideCondition yields G.
667083.role: Extract the selection, base level, columns, rank and divisibility inputs, and pass the period, local and global fields to the shape.

338835.name: GlobalTheory.FinalJoin.runHolds_of_parOK
338835.title: Uniform threshold for admissible runs
338835.statement: There is a common threshold function beyond which the run estimates hold whenever the model laws, injectivity hypothesis and parameter conditions at all in-range indices are satisfied.
338835.role: The caller chooses this threshold function to produce constants for its simultaneous hypothesis and conclusion at each run index.

385779.name: GlobalTheory.GreenBridge.green_of_regular
385779.title: Regular characters yield the Green input
385779.role: Use Frobenius conjugacy of regular labels to associate finite general-linear-group characters to irreducible polynomial labels.

660245.name: GlobalTheory.LocalRows.at_choice_alt
660245.title: Siegel–Weil bounds for a family selection
660245.statement: The convergent unitary Siegel–Weil hypothesis gives the loop bound, the off-diagonal bound and the torsion-free condition for each family class and raw bundle selection.
660245.role: The caller takes the three projections separately to establish the corresponding bounds and torsion-free condition for an entire slot.

660243.name: GlobalTheory.LocalRows.lg1_sLp_sO_hTF
660243.title: Loop, order and torsion-free conditions
660243.statement: Convergence of the unitary Siegel–Weil formula gives large-base witnesses for the loop, order and torsion-free slot conditions for each specified pair of slots and bundle linkage.
660243.role: The caller installs the three conclusions as its loop, order and torsion-free fields.

660244.name: GlobalTheory.LocalRows.sLp_sO_hTF_of_siegelWeil
660244.title: Siegel–Weil gives three local row conditions
660244.statement: Convergent unitary Siegel–Weil implies the Lp, order and torsion-free row conditions for every slot and bundle linkage.
660244.role: The caller projects the three conclusions into its three large-base row witnesses.

661690.name: GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl.exists_baseLattice_of_pair_alt
661690.title: Linked bundles from paired norm extensions
661690.statement: Given compatible norm extensions, level-three and passage data, and the stated elliptic, local Langlands and multiplicity hypotheses, the first extension satisfies membership and admits linked bundles on a large base.
661690.role: The caller takes the pair to be the origin extension and the geometric norm extension and supplies their compatibility data.

661691.name: GlobalTheory.Mem.Top.Bl.exists_baseLattice_of_prime_alt
661691.title: Membership and linked large-base bundles
661691.statement: The stated elliptic, covering, saturation, local Langlands and multiplicity hypotheses together with HypAAlt give membership and a large base with linked bundles for each dependence parameter.
661691.role: The public base-lattice theorem exposes this same pair of conclusions under the same hypotheses.

662130.name: GlobalTheory.MiTop.famAllQ_of_allTrue_alt
662130.title: Compatible geometric rows and columns
662130.statement: Given rapid decay, discrete-series coverage, Harish–Chandra module theory and strong approximation, the family conditions, lower bound on rS and surjectivity assumption produce compatible rows, columns and linked data for the real package.
662130.role: The caller exposes the assembled data as its geometric family-row theorem.

663034.name: GlobalTheory.NLinkClose.main_alt_alt
663034.title: Uniform hub bounds from family estimates
663034.statement: Under the arithmetic hypotheses, twist condition, family facts with nonnegative constant and bound at two and three, sufficiently large family members satisfying the odd finiteness condition admit hub data with a uniform bound.
663034.role: The caller re-exports this implication as its family conclusion from the bound at two and three.

667041.name: GlobalTheory.Svd.servH_row_linkR_alt
667041.title: Artin reciprocity controls selected boundary kernels
667041.statement: Global Artin reciprocity supplies the twist and pointwise kernel conditions for good slots equipped with the boundary reciprocity linkage.
667041.role: The caller re-exports this kernel row as the reciprocity-kernel theorem.

452144.name: GlobalTheory.Svd.servH_row_of_artin
452144.title: Twisting and kernel conditions from reciprocity
452144.statement: With global Artin reciprocity, a slot admitting the required position and a linked row of standard kernel witnesses give both family twisting and pointwise kernel conditions.
452144.role: The caller exports this general implication for standard kernels under Artin reciprocity.

452145.name: GlobalTheory.T.bundle_bothParts_of_standardKernel_of_globalArtinReciprocity
452145.title: Twist and orbit conditions for standard kernels
452145.statement: With global Artin reciprocity, a slot admitting the specified parts and a linked row of standard tied kernels satisfy the twist and orbit conditions in ServH.
452145.role: The caller instantiates the kernel with the boundary-reciprocity kernel and supplies the parts and standard ties for its good slot.

663038.name: GlobalTheory.T.conclF_of_family_facts_and_bound_at_two_three
663038.title: Local bounds for a twisted family
663038.statement: For a good twisted family, the arithmetic hypotheses, family facts with a nonnegative bound, and local bounds at 2 and 3 yield uniform eventual bounds and admissibility data for members satisfying the odd Sha finiteness condition.
663038.role: The caller applies the conclusion along a family to obtain the η-sum estimate.

731923.name: GlobalTheory.T.final_theorem_of_inputs_right
731923.title: Good towers from toroidal and height data
731923.statement: The toroidal compatibility, height, intersection, quotient and theta-uniformization hypotheses in the statement yield existence of good root towers and a uniform volume estimate.
731923.role: The caller supplies the required geometric and arithmetic inputs to obtain the two tower and volume conclusions together.

726489.name: GlobalTheory.T.good_tower_volume_theorem
726489.title: Good root towers and a uniform volume bound
726489.statement: The geometric package, integrability and avoidance hypotheses, Weil condition, positive-family existence and comparison pair imply the good-tower and volume theorems.
726489.role: The reduced-input theorem assembles those six premises and applies this result to recover both conclusions.

666520.name: GlobalTheory.T.hServ_of_linkR
666520.title: Reciprocity supplies the linked selection condition
666520.statement: Global Artin reciprocity gives the family-service row on good parameters whenever the chosen bundle linkage implies the boundary reciprocity linkage.
666520.role: The caller supplies that linkage implication and installs the resulting row as the service field of its definite-side package.

664638.name: GlobalTheory.T.large_unramified_exponent_bundles_exist_alt
664638.title: Mass ratio and large-base bundle existence
664638.statement: For an eventually large retwisting condition, the third-place unitary hypotheses, rationality row and local parameter input give the CM Siegel mass ratio, the membership conditions and a large base carrying linked bundles.
664638.role: The definite-side construction extracts the three components separately when assembling its hypotheses.

664498.name: GlobalTheory.T.main_theorem_from_published_results_alt_alt_alt_alt
664498.title: Period identity for a single coefficient space
664498.statement: Under the listed representation-theoretic hypotheses, a real package satisfying the family conditions, the lower bound on rS and the Pu nonvanishing condition admits isometric period data with nonzero coefficients.
664498.role: The caller obtains the required family conditions from a true package and applies this result to prove its period condition.

664500.name: GlobalTheory.T.main_theorem_from_published_results_alt_alt_alt_alt_alt
664500.title: Isometric periods from a real package
664500.statement: Under the stated representation-theoretic premises, the compatibility conditions on a real package, a positive rank parameter and nonvanishing local period values yield the package’s isometric period identity with nonzero coefficients.
664500.role: The caller applies this result separately to the package of each bundle to build a row of period identities.

664502.name: GlobalTheory.T.main_theorem_published_inputs_third_alt_alt
664502.title: Linked period identities and multiplicities
664502.statement: The listed representation-theoretic and Siegel–Weil inputs produce both linked isometric period identities with nonzero coefficients and the linked multiplicity condition for each parameter extension.
664502.role: The open-parameter proof uses the first component in its intermediate construction and the second as its multiplicity field.

664503.name: GlobalTheory.T.main_theorem_published_inputs_variant_alt_alt
664503.title: Isometric period identities for linked bundles
664503.statement: Given the listed representation-theoretic inputs, a diagonal scale-and-rank condition and witnesses at each parameter point, good linked bundles satisfy the period identity with norm-preserving data and nonzero coefficients.
664503.role: The caller specializes this bundle result while constructing linked period and multiplicity conditions.

664505.name: GlobalTheory.T.main_theorem_published_results_final_alt_alt
664505.title: Inner-product identity across a bundle row
664505.statement: The listed representation-theoretic inputs, diagonal bounds, pointwise witnesses and bundle conditions yield the inner-product identity with norm-preserving data and nonzero factors throughout the row.
664505.role: The closing lemma discharges the bundle-point premise from cusp rapid decay and the accompanying representation hypotheses.

661689.name: GlobalTheory.T.member_exists_baseLattice_alt
661689.title: Membership and linked bundles for origin extensions
661689.statement: Under the elliptic, multiplicity, saturation, local Langlands and other stated hypotheses, the origin extension has the membership properties and a large-base condition supporting linked bundles.
661689.role: The caller extracts the membership half and transports it to the extension with an additional pointwise property.

665157.name: GlobalTheory.T.open0_of_unitary_group_hypotheses
665157.title: Unitary inputs give open parameter conditions
665157.statement: The third-place unitary-group hypotheses give the open parameter package, including primitivity, divisor and multiplicity conditions, for each local-parameter witness and real dependence parameter.
665157.role: The caller transports this package to its stronger extension before assembling the rows needed on the definite side.

667042.name: GlobalTheory.T.reciprocity_kernel_of_artin
667042.title: Artin reciprocity controls boundary kernels
667042.statement: Global Artin reciprocity gives both the family twisting condition and the pointwise kernel conditions on the reciprocity-linked row of good parameters.
667042.role: The caller uses the map from a linked bundle to its reciprocity boundary to transport the two conditions.

662131.name: GlobalTheory.T.true_geometry_family_row_data_alt
662131.title: Central pinning element and family characters
662131.statement: Given the four automorphic inputs, the initial family conditions, a positive rank parameter and the surjectivity hypothesis, there is a common central element with character and descent data for each index.
662131.role: The caller derives surjectivity from its theta and doubling inputs, then invokes this package in the proof of the inner-product identity.

727319.name: GlobalTheory.T.volume_theorem_of_inputs
727319.title: Uniform tower volume and slope bounds
727319.statement: Under the stated integrability, Weil, Hodge flag, degree, twisting and comparison inputs, one constant gives the tower volume theorem, including the mean-slope estimate, for all models satisfying its hypotheses.
727319.role: The tower construction supplies geometric height constants and Hodge data to obtain the volume half of its two conclusions.

664504.name: GlobalTheory.miStarRowClosing_alt_alt
664504.title: Isometric period identities on linked bundles
664504.statement: The representation-theoretic inputs, a diagonal rank-and-scale condition and nonempty auxiliary witnesses at each parameter point give a row of isometric period identities with nonzero coefficients.
664504.role: The published-input variant re-exports the period-identity row with the same diagonal and witness assumptions.

664501.name: GlobalTheory.miStarRow_alt_alt
664501.title: Linked period identities with eventual multiplicity
664501.statement: The stated representation-theoretic inputs and the convergent unitary Siegel–Weil formula yield both the pointwise period-identity row and its eventual multiplicity row at the linked extension parameters.
664501.role: The third published-input theorem re-exports this conjunction for extension parameters.

666519.name: GlobalTheory.row_hServ_of_link_alt
666519.title: Twist and orbit data from reciprocity linkage
666519.statement: Global Artin reciprocity gives the twist-system and orbit conditions for selections in a good slot whenever the bundle linkage implies the prescribed reciprocity linkage.
666519.role: The exported reciprocity-link theorem uses this implication directly for an arbitrary compatible linkage.

780726.name: PositivityTheory.HtPt.Ah.deep_slim_use
780726.title: Uniform lower bound for mean volume slopes
780726.statement: The resolution, principalisation, Poincaré–Lelong, Hilbert–Samuel, bigness, Hodge–Tate and arithmetic hypotheses give a uniform lower bound for weighted mean component slopes on the specified deep models with at most fifteen prime factors in the level parameter.
780726.role: The covolume-bound proof uses this estimate as its deep-model input.

854871.name: PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2
854871.title: Theta integral agreement and local matching
854871.statement: The Eisenstein-series hypothesis and standard Siegel–Weil formula supply both agreement of theta integrals and the existence of matching local data.
854871.role: The literature-input theorem extracts these two premises from its package and passes them to this result.

854870.name: PositivityTheory.ThKR.theoremK_head2_of_mod
854870.title: Theta matching from the spherical modulus condition
854870.statement: The spherical modulus condition together with the Eisenstein and Siegel–Weil inputs implies agreement of theta integrals and the local matching statement.
854870.role: The caller supplies the spherical modulus result and leaves the Eisenstein and Siegel–Weil inputs explicit.

667817.name: SelfIntersectionVolumeEstimates.topCovolG_alt_alt
667817.title: Eventual covolume bound for families
667817.statement: The stated volume, geometric, Hodge-bundle, deformation and intersection hypotheses imply that the covolume inequality holds eventually at all family points for every sufficiently large parameter.
667817.role: The caller builds the geometric and height hypotheses from its toroidal and arithmetic assumptions and passes them to this covolume estimate.

667818.name: SelfIntersectionVolumeEstimates.topCovolSlim2_use_alt_alt
667818.title: Produce the covolume bound
667818.statement: The named geometric, arithmetic Hilbert–Samuel and Hodge-bundle hypotheses imply CovolumeBoundOfX.
667818.role: This supplies the covolume comparison used by the seven-input theorem. Its source signature lists the geometric and arithmetic hypotheses.
667818.caption: Covolume estimates from arithmetic intersection theory

656519.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.core_gm
656519.title: From the height discrepancy to the prime sum
656519.statement: For large x, EAtH and CoreAtH imply G_P(x)≤x^(1/2+(eD+eL+7)ε).
656519.role: Bound the per-index discrepancy, average via the character estimate and absorb the level-dependent factor into x^ε.

656530.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.formB
656530.title: The analytic criterion for a level
656530.statement: For every level, every λ>1 and 0<θ<1, arbitrarily late windows bounded by x^θ imply no zero right of θ.
656530.role: Translate the level to a finite character family with positive weights. Apply the power-window theorem with δ=λ−1 and C=1.

656538.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.level_gm_le_on_family_scales
656538.title: The prime-sum inequality on tied families
656538.statement: For every level, tied compatible families yield the windowed upper bound on the weighted prime sum.
656538.role: Translate ChainTied into the shared host data and call the Artin-input window theorem.

656572.name: UpperTheory.Comparison₂.windowInequality_of_artinInputs
656572.title: Estimate the weighted level on a window
656572.statement: Identification of tied families with controlled host data gives ChebyshevInequalityOnWindows at any level.
656572.role: Choose thresholds for the arithmetic and family estimates and obtain a compatible witness at each scale in the window.

607158.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter
607158.title: Closed half-plane assembly
607158.statement: EveryCharacter with no explicit arithmetic premise.
607158.role: The final line supplies a named producer for the local–global Galois row.
607158.caption: Zero-free half-plane for Dirichlet L-functions

607157.name: UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row
607157.title: The half-plane theorem from one row
607157.statement: Row0b with the specified local parameter convention implies EveryCharacter.
607157.role: The same h fills two fields in the literature-input record and produces the cohomological window.

631204.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geoOne_holds
631204.title: Weight-one geometric realization
631204.role: Converts the stated weight-one realization into the geometric input to the row.

630282.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.geometric_realization_of_weight_one
630282.title: Weight-one Galois representations from geometry
630282.statement: Assuming the holomorphic Lefschetz formula, the weight-one construction gives Galois representations over CM fields with the prescribed local properties, including crystalline realizations at qualifying places above the chosen prime.
630282.role: The caller supplies the holomorphic Lefschetz input to obtain the weight-one realization package.

630280.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.kodaira_spencer_of_weight_one
630280.title: Kodaira–Spencer data for weight-one realization
630280.statement: Assuming the holomorphic Lefschetz formula, the theorem supplies the full Kodaira–Spencer package, including the congruence and Hodge conditions.
630280.role: The weight-one realization takes this package together with the geometric steps and the tower plan.

630279.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.Geo.steps_holds
630279.title: Geometric steps for weight-one realization
630279.statement: The geometric steps package provides representation existence, crystalline and jump conditions, Frobenius data and the accompanying conditions on twists.
630279.role: The weight-one realization combines this package with the Kodaira–Spencer conditions and the tower plan.
630279.caption: Frobenius and crystalline data in weight one

631235.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter
631235.title: Producer of the Galois row
631235.statement: Row0b recT with no explicit global premise.
631235.role: Feed the named theta-lift theorem to the conditional Galois construction.

630050.name: UpperTheory.Gal.Int.galoisRepresentations_of_thetaLift
630050.title: Galois representations from theta lifting
630050.role: Apply the geometric realization theorem with the named weight-one source and the theta lift.

660540.name: UpperTheory.GalC.final_alt_alt
660540.title: Local arithmetic yields the η-sum bound
660540.statement: Under the stated arithmetic and Galois hypotheses, including local duality and depth-zero support, a linked family bound at 2 and 3 implies a linked uniform η-sum estimate.
660540.role: The caller transports this estimate to its extended parameters to build the definite-side hypothesis package.

663917.name: UpperTheory.GalC.final_of_alt
663917.title: Cut and Galois data control η-sums
663917.statement: Given the cut, Galois, third-layer and depth-zero hypotheses, a linked family bound at 2 and 3 implies the linked η-sum estimate for the parameters of dependence.
663917.role: The caller supplies the cut and Galois hypotheses from its arithmetic inputs to close the family estimate.

663918.name: UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_boundAtTwoThree_slot
663918.title: From local bounds to the family η-sum estimate
663918.statement: Under the arithmetic and cut hypotheses, a slot carrying Galois preconditions and the four tie conditions converts the family bound at two and three into the eventual LinkN estimate on η-sums.
663918.role: The caller applies the slot implication to its parameter-dependent linked data to obtain the linked family estimate.

663915.name: UpperTheory.GalC.linkN_of_twGood_galoisPreconditions
663915.title: Uniform bounds for lift η-sums
663915.statement: For a twist-good family, the cut and Galois hypotheses with Tie4 give a uniform eventual η-sum estimate for each eligible lift, subject to the finiteness and summability conditions in LinkN.
663915.role: The caller applies the estimate to each qualifying family after extracting twist goodness and the pointwise Galois conditions from its slot hypotheses.

663916.name: UpperTheory.GalC.linkedAt_linkN_of_boundAtTwoThree
663916.title: Linked local bounds control η-sums
663916.statement: For fixed parameters, linked Galois and compatibility data together with linked bounds at 2 and 3 yield a linked η-sum estimate under the cut and arithmetic hypotheses.
663916.role: The caller transports the Galois and compatibility witnesses to the required parameters, then applies this implication.

647570.name: UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b
647570.title: The local–global Galois row
647570.statement: For a regular algebraic polarized cuspidal representation over a CM field and a prime ℓ, there exist a Galois representation, weight and Hodge–Tate multiset satisfying PropsB.
647570.role: The fields of PropsB specify continuity, semisimplicity, comparisons and weight relations.

667329.name: UpperTheory.Lit.every_character_of_theta_integrals_local_matching
667329.title: Seven inputs for every character
667329.statement: The seven groups of hypotheses imply EveryCharacter.
667329.role: Construct the definite-side package, obtain a Green-character input, and invoke the primitive-to-all-character assembly.
667329.caption: Theta matching and covolume imply nonvanishing

667330.name: UpperTheory.Lit.nonempty_hyps_definite_side_of_closed_bound
667330.title: Build a nonempty definite-side package
667330.statement: Unitary, theta, matching, covolume, local-parameter and linked-bound data yield Nonempty (HypsAlt … DefiniteSideCondition).
667330.role: Use test vectors, Fourier coefficient grids, linked bundles and a single choice of the maximum of two thresholds.
667330.caption: Test vectors and Fourier bounds on the definite side

661472.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.OpenLiteratureStatements
661472.title: Three fields in the literature input
661472.statement: The record has fields Row, RecTExists and Row, in that order.
661472.role: The two row fields have the same Lean type. The closed caller inserts the same term in both places.

661565.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.every_character_of_literature_of_vWin
661565.title: Assemble the automorphic inputs
661565.role: Pass the eigenvalue and local-theta packages, local matching, covolumes, local Langlands and VWin to the seven-input implication.
661565.caption: Dirichlet nonvanishing from the cohomological window

661603.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.local_langlands_gl_recT_exists_of_literature
661603.title: The local parameter input at the call site
661603.statement: OpenLiteratureStatements imply RecTExists in the GL convention.
661603.role: Apply the local correspondence comparison to the parameter field of O and the named local converse, depth-zero, reciprocity and multisegment ingredients.

661655.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.local_langlands_recT_exists_of_literature
661655.title: Read the parameter field
661655.role: Project the localLanglandsExists field of O.

661592.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_arithmetic
661592.title: The Hodge-bundle package
661592.role: The geometric record starts with toroidal compactification, volume, arithmetic intersection calculus and abelian de Rham data. It feeds the covolume producer.

661642.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_eigen
661642.title: The unitary and eigenvalue package
661642.role: The record starts with cohomological, finite-field character, Hecke, Chebotarev, polarized Galois and base-change inputs. These are the P argument.

661548.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.published_results_first
661548.title: The local theta package
661548.role: The record begins with Green series, Linnik, complex multiplication, mirabolic, branching and local representation inputs. These supply F.

661533.name: UpperTheory.LiteratureTheorems.theta_integrals_agree_and_local_matching_of_literature
661533.title: Match global integrals and local data
661533.role: Theorem K combines Eisenstein-series and Siegel–Weil inputs to produce both comparison statements.

660241.name: UpperTheory.N.boundAtTwoThree_linked_of_recT
660241.title: Bind the estimates at 2 and 3
660241.statement: For local-global inputs, RecTExists and a compatible dependence parameter, the bounds at two and three hold on linked data.
660241.role: Package the local bounds for every eligible family into a linked slot at this common parameter.

587005.name: UpperTheory.One.Join.automorphic_window_of_inputs
587005.title: Supply the automorphic window inputs
587005.statement: OpenImageCondition, BaseChangeIsobaricN and RowT imply VWin.
587005.role: Add the CM abelian inputs to the depth-zero residual base-change argument.

587003.name: UpperTheory.One.Join.v_window_of_depth_zero_residual_bc_cm
587003.title: Build the rank-N package
587003.statement: The open-image, base-change, Galois and CM packages imply VWin.
587003.role: Package local, automorphic, cohomological and CM inputs for the rank-N theorem.

587298.name: UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row
587298.title: Cohomological window from the row
587298.statement: Row0b in the stated convention implies VWin.
587298.role: Pass an open-image record, the base-change theorem and the Galois row to the automorphic window construction.
587298.caption: Cohomological windows from Galois compatibility

646008.name: UpperTheory.TP.K.tLiftK
646008.title: Theta-lift existence at high rank
646008.statement: For the admissible CM data of TLiftK, for all sufficiently high dimensions and allowed weights a lift U′ exists.
646008.role: This named theorem supplies the high-dimensional lift required for Row0b.

642594.name: UpperTheory.TP.TLiftK
642594.title: Quantifiers of the theta lift
642594.statement: For each admissible CM setup, n≥1 and X, there exists d₀; for each d≥d₀, permissible W, Hecke characters, weights and U, an IsLift witness U′ exists.
642594.role: The weight inequality is imposed after the choice of d. The lift has an explicit existential codomain.

607123.name: UpperTheory.Top.VVle
607123.title: Weighted lengths of local-global kernels
607123.statement: For all admissible local data, lengths are finite for 1≤e<t and every finite prime sum of log(ℓ) times the sum of these lengths is ≤B.
607123.role: Finiteness precedes conversion of an extended natural length to an ordinary natural.

607100.name: UpperTheory.Top.VWinAt
607100.title: The cohomological window
607100.statement: For every ε∈(0,1/52) and admissible layer choice e(x), sufficiently large X and each prescribed pair q,d admit a window [Y,Y²] where VAt holds.
607100.role: The endpoint uses Ct=401. VAt bounds twists below floor(x^401) by sqrt(exp(x^ε)).

607087.name: UpperTheory.Top.divinN_of_hypV
607087.title: Control the local divisibility loss
607087.statement: For ε>0, HypV, LinkN and SmallLevelRankEq imply DIVinN on the family.
607087.role: Bound the weighted cohomology sum, replace the rank and absorb log²x into x^ε.

667822.name: UpperTheory.Top.every_character_of_green_v_win
667822.title: Pass from primitive to all characters
667822.statement: Green ∧ VWin ∧ nonempty definite-side hypotheses imply EveryCharacter, written as three binders.
667822.role: Obtain primitive nonvanishing at cyclic levels and restore imprimitive factors.

607145.name: UpperTheory.Top.imprimitive
607145.title: Restore all characters
607145.statement: ZeroFreeAll for primitive characters implies the all-moduli right-half-plane assertion with the principal pole exception.
607145.role: Use the change-of-level formula and nonvanishing of all finitely many additional Euler factors.

667853.name: UpperTheory.Top.shape_closed_link_n_of_green
667853.title: Choose a common geometric family
667853.statement: Green implies the specified TopShapeAlt ending in TopG.
667853.role: Calls topDesWin with Cabs=2, C0=3, eD=2 and eL=0. This fixes both analytic loss exponents.

607278.name: UpperTheory.Top.supplyChi
607278.title: Produce cyclic character hosts
607278.statement: For every primitive ψ, VWinAt ψ 401 implies host existence at width 3/2.
607278.role: Use the window for the chosen character, then admissible twisted character classes on sufficiently large scales.

607080.name: UpperTheory.Top.topDesWin
607080.title: Combine divisibility, slopes and windows
607080.statement: The listed existence, local, rank, divisibility, global and slope controls produce FamilyClassConnected.
607080.role: Construct one family after taking a common epsilon threshold. Its loss exponents are the given eD and eL.

607086.name: UpperTheory.Top.vvRecord
607086.title: Sum the local losses
607086.statement: VVle gives finite cohomology lengths, summability and the bound on the infinite sum of vvTerm.
607086.role: Apply the bounded-partial-sums criterion to nonnegative prime contributions.

607297.name: UpperTheory.Top.zeroFreeAll_of_topG
607297.title: Produce primitive zero-free levels
607297.statement: For λ>1, TopG and hosts for every primitive character imply ZeroFreeAll.
607297.role: Combine the host supply, bound on tied families and the analytic criterion at each cyclic level.

667823.name: UpperTheory.Top.zero_free_all_of_green_v_win
667823.title: Select the window width 3/2
667823.statement: Green, VWin and a nonempty definite-side package imply ZeroFreeAll.
667823.role: Eliminate the nonempty package. Its shape supplies TopG and VWin supplies hosts for each primitive character.

556316.name: UpperTheory.V.FW.ferreroWashington
556316.title: Uniform ℓ-rank of class groups in the tower
556316.statement: For each eligible abelian base K and prime ℓ there is an exponent r bounding the order of the quotient by ℓ-th powers by ℓʳ on every cyclotomic layer.
556316.role: Embed the abelian base into a cyclotomic field. Use the cyclotomic index estimate and descend across a uniformly bounded degree. The root-of-unity premise in the published interface is unused by this proof.

584661.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.Core.of_four_alt
584661.title: Combine the cohomology counts
584661.statement: Rank-N input, an existential K bound and CountI, CountII, CountIII, CountV imply VWin.
584661.role: Use local cohomological estimates, Ferrero–Washington and the additional terms in vwin_of_counts.

583634.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.countII_and_countIII_of_printsH_of_sp4In
583634.title: Cases II and III from the rank-four symplectic argument
583634.statement: Cases II and III have uniform polynomial bounds for each normalized character length, with finiteness. The hypotheses distinguish parity of character orders and divisibility of twice the twist.
583634.role: Supply the symplectic rigidity and eigensystem-counting inputs to the same rank-four theorem. The cohomological hypotheses and LemmaK provide the finite local lengths used in its two outputs.

585878.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.sp4In0_alt
585878.title: Automorphy at irreducible symplectic lifts
585878.statement: The stated arithmetic package gives the finiteness and block-image conditions of the four-dimensional symplectic case and a complex embedding under which every eligible irreducible lift satisfies its automorphy condition.
585878.role: The caller uses this symplectic input to derive its second and third counting bounds together.

587393.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.v_window_of_automorphy_csd_ss_mono_odd
587393.title: Pass through the descent hypotheses
587393.role: Combine the rank-N input with the weak descent theorem and the package produced by patching.

587394.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.DescentVanishingReductions.vwin_of_hypotheses_H_E_alt
587394.title: Produce the four counting bounds
587394.role: Build the K bound, the descent inputs and counting cases I, II, III and V.
587394.caption: Cohomological windows from four counting bounds

560715.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.jointWin_of_counts
560715.title: Reuse the tower interval for the positive part
560715.statement: For each eligible choice of character and parameters, one interval satisfies both the tower and positive-part bounds at every point.
560715.role: Apply the height estimate to the very interval selected by ThmBab. Its universal quantifier over accepted windows permits this reuse.

560716.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.pointHV_of_counts
560716.title: Combine the two prime sums at a point
560716.statement: After the character and layer indices are fixed, one polynomial bound controls the positive cohomological sum on eligible hosts, with an additive multiple of the layer budget.
560716.role: Form separate sums inside and outside the fixed exceptional set. Inside, the dispatcher also supplies Case IV and the strict-threshold case Vs. Add the two estimates using the same host and layer budget.

560607.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.sumIn
560607.title: Add contributions inside the exceptional set
560607.statement: For fixed character, exceptional coefficient prime and layer index, the positive-part sum at that prime is at most (Nt)^C + C·B when the fixed layer satisfies its budget B.
560607.role: Separate the twist-one threshold from the higher twists. For the odd-order branch, Case IV uses the supplied layer bound. Absorb the finite character contributions into a common exponent.

560788.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.sumOut
560788.title: Bound the sum over arbitrary finite sets of other primes
560788.statement: Choose a common exponent and two auxiliary primes before the host. The positive-part sum over every allowed finite set of nonexceptional odd primes is at most (Nt)^C.
560788.role: Apply Case I to the unrestricted contribution. For the remainder ℓ−1 divides twice the twist, bounding the number of relevant primes. Cases Z, II and III and the character counts control these terms.

560714.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.thmHV_of_counts
560714.title: Evaluate the pointwise estimate on admissible windows
560714.statement: Every package K and positive cutoff exponent Ct satisfy the positive-part height theorem under the stated counting and cohomology inputs.
560714.role: First prove the estimate with layer bounds as hypotheses. The height theorem specializes it using the supplied interval, the primes, the cutoff and the very same field.

560713.name: UpperTheory.V.HV.vwin_of_counts
560713.title: Convert the joint window into VWin
560713.statement: The tower window, sign bounds and five counting inputs yield VWin, the cohomology estimate for each primitive character at cutoff exponent 401.
560713.role: Obtain a common tower and positive-part window, convert the negative-part bound at exponent 401, and combine the contributions on the same interval.

541794.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.aBound_of_descends
541794.title: Control exceptional twists by the fixed layer
541794.statement: The lengths are controlled by at most R ℓ-adic centres. For all twists they are also bounded by the fixed-layer H² length plus R times the excess layer index.
541794.role: Use unipotence modulo ℓ and the generator bound for the centres. The relative growth estimate can allow infinite length at a singular twist. Descent and duality bound the reference value by the arithmetic H² length.

541795.name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.aBound_of_isTower
541795.title: From a finitely generated tower to two length bounds
541795.statement: For each prime and eligible tower, ABound consists of a bound away from finitely many centres and a bound in terms of a fixed layer.
541795.role: Choose a Galois element generating the cyclotomic direction, prove the descent equality for its twists, and apply the two cokernel estimates on the tower module.

562560.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.thmBab_of
562560.title: Choose one set of tower constants
562560.statement: There exists a single BConst K such that every Ct ≥ 1 satisfies ThmBab K Ct.
562560.role: Choose the uniform two-adic rank and the ranks of the eligible odd-prime towers before the scale and auxiliary prime pair. Unite the exceptional twists and find a single interval avoiding their forbidden ranges.

562561.name: UpperTheory.V.Win.thmBab_of_lemmaK
562561.title: Assemble the arithmetic tower window
562561.statement: One package of constants works at every cutoff exponent Ct ≥ 1.
562561.role: Apply the cohomological bound to each eligible tower. Ferrero–Washington supplies the generator bounds for the fixed odd primes and the varying two-adic bases. Pass both estimates and the uniform H² bound to the window construction.

584932.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.count_i_of_printed_bound_k_kato_automorphy
584932.title: Case I gives one bound across coefficient primes
584932.statement: Away from the exceptional set, when ℓ−1 does not divide twice the twist, the sum over every allowed finite set of coefficient primes obeys one polynomial bound.
584932.role: Combine a rank-three eigensystem count with a single-character rigidity bound. Their common integer bounds the local lengths by its valuations. Two auxiliary primes then cover all the coefficient primes.

584931.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.count_v_of_printed_bound_k_reduced_unitary_lift
584931.title: Case V at twist one
584931.statement: For exceptional odd primes at twist one, Case V bounds the normalized length when the two-adic conductor crosses the specified threshold, including equality.
584931.role: Pass a reduced unitary lift, local and global cohomological estimates, host rigidity and a host parameter count to the rank-three inertia argument. The strict reverse threshold is covered by a separate case.

584517.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.J.propGK_of_numberU3U_of_oneCharU
584517.title: A nonzero integer controls one character orbit
584517.statement: For a fixed imaginary quadratic field, twist, character kernel and admissible auxiliary prime, one nonzero integer gives a logarithmic size bound and simultaneous valuation bounds at the other eligible primes.
584517.role: Make a Galois-stable family of characters with the chosen kernel. A trace product supplies the integer before the coefficient prime is chosen. Rigidity bounds the sum of the orbit lengths by twice its valuation.

576583.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.Kato.Final.zetaUr
576583.title: An unramified integral Kato cocycle
576583.statement: For an admissible two-dimensional representation and newform satisfying the specified unramified source hypotheses, there is an integral unramified cocycle with the prescribed non-Greenberg and tame conditions.
576583.role: The caller combines this existence theorem with its comparison hypothesis to obtain ordinary Bloch–Kato Selmer vanishing.

584789.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.Kato.WeilSphericalRecords.katoTwoW_of_printsH
584789.title: Kato vanishing for two Selmer groups
584789.statement: Under the stated arithmetic package, an admissible two-dimensional representation with the required newform and witness has vanishing Bloch–Kato Selmer groups for itself and its character twist.
584789.role: The window proof feeds this two-twist vanishing result into the first of its counting bounds.

584790.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.Kato.WeilSphericalRecords.katoTwoW_of_printsH_of_rT_of_quadBC2
584790.title: Two Selmer vanishings from quadratic base change
584790.statement: The packaged arithmetic hypotheses, Galois row and quadratic base change imply Bloch–Kato Selmer vanishing for both the trivial and character twists of a two-dimensional representation satisfying the specified newform and witness conditions.
584790.role: The caller supplies the Galois row from its classical hypotheses and inserts the quadratic base-change theorem.

576167.name: UpperTheory.V.Z.Kato.WeilSphericalRecords.twoS
576167.title: Selmer vanishing for two twists
576167.statement: Given the cohomology and spherical-source hypotheses, the specified two-dimensional newform representation satisfies Bloch–Kato Selmer vanishing for both the trivial twist and the twist by θ.
576167.role: The caller supplies the cohomology and source inputs, reducing the remaining step to the spherical condition.

584785.name: UpperTheory.V.ZK.lemmaK_litN_alt
584785.title: Supply the absolute bound for the reference layer
584785.statement: One real exponent bounds the logarithm of the order of H²(G_{L,S}, ℤℓ(e+1)) over all eligible fields, coefficient primes and positive twists. Each such group is finite.
584785.role: Insert the odd-degree integral homology rank estimate into the reduction from the rank-N package. The resulting LemmaK bound may be applied at the fixed layer even when the abstract cokernel estimate allows infinite length.

587392.name: UpperTheory.V.v_window_of_literal_automorphy_n
587392.title: Window from rank-N automorphy
587392.role: Invoke the automorphy-and-descent reduction for this rank-N package.

649562.name: UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.recTExists
649562.title: Existence of local Langlands parameters
649562.role: Extend a parameter from the cuspidal representations and establish the local comparison fields.

872704.name: _private.Formalism.GL3MeanSquares.HookFormulaTorsion.PsiZeroIntegral.0.Formalism.HermitianLattices.P.PsiZeroIntegral.core_tendsto
872704.title: Pass the Mellin integral to σ = 1
872704.statement: A logarithmic remainder bound lets σ times the weighted integral tend to its value at σ=1 from the right.
872704.role: The local integrand is measurable. A bound by the integrable error at σ=1 gives dominated convergence. The factor σ tends to one.

872699.name: _private.Formalism.GL3MeanSquares.HookFormulaTorsion.PsiZeroIntegral.0.Formalism.HermitianLattices.P.PsiZeroIntegral.psiZeroConst_main
872699.title: Match the two limits at one
872699.statement: For the trivial character modulo one the Chebyshev remainder has first moment −1−γ.
872699.role: Evaluate the Mellin integral for real σ>1 in terms of the logarithmic derivative of zeta. The remainder bound allows passage to σ=1. The finite part of the logarithmic derivative fixes the value.

872695.name: _private.Formalism.GL3MeanSquares.HookFormulaTorsion.PsiZeroIntegral.0.Formalism.HermitianLattices.P.PsiZeroIntegral.sw_bound
872695.title: Dominate the centered character sum
872695.statement: For each fixed character, the centered von Mangoldt sum is eventually bounded in norm by Kt/log²t.
872695.role: The Siegel–Walfisz estimate applies at a fixed modulus for all sufficiently large t. Exponential decay in the square root of log t implies the displayed inverse logarithmic factor.

872707.name: _private.Formalism.GL3MeanSquares.HookFormulaTorsion.PsiZeroIntegral.0.Formalism.HermitianLattices.P.PsiZeroIntegral.zeta_logderiv_limit
872707.title: Read Euler’s constant from the logarithmic derivative
872707.statement: As complex s tends puncturedly to 1, ζ′(s)/ζ(s)+1/(s−1) tends to γ.
872707.role: Remove the pole by putting g(s)=(s−1)ζ(s) and g(1)=1. The quotient g′/g tends to γ and agrees with the regularized logarithmic derivative off the pole.

1265238.name: allChi
1265238.title: All-character half-plane theorem
1265238.role: Re-export everyCharacter from the arithmetic development.
1265238.caption: Right-half-plane nonvanishing for all characters
